Rashi on Pesachim 92b:10:1.hebrew: ור' נחמן - דאמר לא תנן אוננין ברישא, ו"לא עשה" אדרך רחוקה קאי, אמר לך: סיפא ודאי "מזיד" מחסרא בה, ועלה קאי "ולא עשה" דסיפא, ו"חייבין" בהכרת נמי עליה קאי. והא דתני "חייבין" לשון רבים — איידי דתנא פטורין, תנא נמי חייבין. (אמר המגיה: בקצת פי' רש"י זה אינו.) ותימה לי: אמאי לא אמר ר"נ "מנא אמינא לה? דקתני: א"כ למה נאמר דרך רחוקה, שאלו פטורין כו'", מדקאמר "למה נאמר" ש"מ דאי בעי למיעבד עביד כר"נ, דאי כרב ששת — איצטריך דאי בעי למיעבד דלא ליעבד. (עד כאן):
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:10:1.english: And Rav Nachman - who says that we did not learn [the case of] acute mourners in the first clause, and [the phrase] "and did not observe" refers to [one on] a distant journey, could say to you: The latter clause is certainly missing [the case of] an intentional [transgressor], and [the phrase] "and did not observe" of the latter clause refers to it, and "are liable" to excision also refers to it. And that which it teaches "are liable" in the plural — since it taught "are exempt" [in the plural], it also taught "are liable" [in the plural]. (The glossator says: In some [editions of] Rashi's commentary, this is not [present].) And I wonder: why did Rav Nachman not say, "From where do I say it? For it teaches: 'If so, why is "a distant journey" stated, since these are exempt, etc.'" — since it says "why is it stated," learn from this that if one wishes to observe [it], he may observe [it], like Rav Nachman; for if [the law were] like Rav Sheshet, [the verse] would be necessary [to teach] that if he wishes to observe [it], he should not observe [it]. (Thus far [the gloss].)

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:1:1.hebrew: שבודקין - מהלכין בבית הפרס ע"י בדיקה לעשות פסח, אם אין לו דרך אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:1:1.english: That we examine - One walks through a beit haperas by means of examination to offer the Paschal lamb, if he has no other route.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:1:2.hebrew: ואין בודקין לאוכלי תרומה - אלא ימתין ויקיף או יום או יומים, עד שמגיע אל תרומתו ואוכלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:1:2.english: And we do not examine for those eating terumah - Rather, he should wait and go around [the beit haperas] for a day or two, until he reaches his terumah and eats it.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג מאי בודקין - היאך יבדוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:1.english: We read: What is [meant by] "we examine" - How should one examine?

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:2.hebrew: מנפח בית הפרס - הוא שדה שנחרש בה קבר, כדתנן (אהלות פי"ז מ"א): החורש בית הקבר, הרי זה עושה בית הפרס מלא מענה, מאה אמה. וגזור רבנן שמא כיתתה מחרישה את העצמות ופיזרתן באורך המענה, ויש כאן עצם כשעורה ויעבור ויסיטנו. ועצם כשעורה מטמאה במגע ובמשא, דהיינו היסט. הלכך מנפחו בפיו: ואם יש עצם גדול, יראנו, ועצם כשעורה נדחה בנפיחתו. ואהל אין מטמאו, דהא אין טומאת אהל בעצמות אלא רוב בנין ורוב מנין:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:2.english: He blows [the dust of] the beit haperas - [A beit haperas] is a field in which a grave was plowed, as we learned in a Mishnah (Ohalot 17:1): "One who plows a grave makes a beit haperas the full length of a furrow, one hundred cubits." And the Rabbis decreed [impurity] lest the plow crushed the bones and scattered them along the length of the furrow, and there is a bone the size of a barleycorn here, and he will pass [over it] and move it. And a bone the size of a barleycorn imparts impurity through contact and through carrying, which is [what happens when] moving [it]. Therefore, he blows it with his mouth: if there is a large bone, he will see it, and a bone the size of a barleycorn is pushed away by his blowing. And [by] overshadowing (ohel) it does not render him impure, for there is no impurity of overshadowing with bones except [when there is] the majority of the [skeletal] structure or the majority of the count [of bones].

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:3.hebrew: שנידש - ברגל, טהור, שדריסת הרגלים העבירתן. והבא לעשות פסחו יבדוק אם נידש ויעבור, אבל לאכילת תרומה לא סמכי' עלה, שיכול להמתין. ובית הפרס מדבריהם, ולא העמידום במקום כרת דפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:2:3.english: That has been trodden - by foot [is] ritually pure, for the treading of feet has removed them [any bone fragments]. And one who comes to offer his Paschal lamb should examine whether [the path] has been trodden, and [if so, he may] pass through; but for eating terumah we do not rely on it, for he can wait. And [the impurity of] a beit haperas is by rabbinic decree, and [the Sages] did not uphold their [decree] in a case involving karet for the Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:4:1.hebrew: מי שהיה טמא: א"כ למה נאמר טמא - בגמ' פריך: הא איצטריך, דאי בעי למיעבד בראשון לא מצי עביד. אלא אדרך רחוקה קאי, דאנוס הוי דלא מצי עביד — וה"נ אמרינן בגמרא — ואי בעי למיעבד ע"י שלוחו עביד, כמ"ד בגמרא הורצה. והלכך, הואיל ושאר אונסין אידחו לשני, אונס דדרך רחוקה ל"ל דאידכר רחמנא טפי מאונס אחרינא? הא דרך רחוקה אנוס הוא שאינו יכול ליכנס כל שעת שחיטה, כדאמרינן בגמ', ולאשמעינן דאי בעי למיעבד לא מצי עביד לא מצינו למימר, דהא ודאי מצי עביד כמ"ד הורצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:4:1.english: One who was [ritually] impure: If so, why is "impure" stated - In the Gemara it asks: Surely [it] is necessary, for if he wanted to offer [it] on the first [Pesaḥ], he could not offer [it]! Rather, [the Mishnah's question] refers to "a distant journey," for he is under constraint such that he cannot offer [it] — and so too we say in the Gemara — and if he wants to offer [it] through his agent, he can offer [it], in accordance with the one who says in the Gemara [that it] is accepted. Therefore, since other constraints are deferred to the second [Pesaḥ], why do I need the constraint of "a distant journey," that the Merciful One mentioned [it] more than another constraint? For "a distant journey" is [a case of] constraint, since he cannot enter [Jerusalem] during the entire time of slaughter, as we say in the Gemara; and we cannot say [that it was written] to teach us that if he wanted to offer [it] he could not offer [it], for he certainly can offer [it] according to the one who says [that it] is accepted.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:4:2.hebrew: שאלו פטורין מן ההכרת - טמא ודרך רחוקה. ושגג ונאנס, ואלו חייבין, מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:4:2.english: That these are exempt from karet - [Namely,] one who was ritually impure or [on] a distant journey. And [as for] one who acted unwittingly or was prevented [by circumstances beyond his control], and [the statement] "and those are liable" — [this] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:5:1.hebrew: שחטו וזרקו עליו - ולערב יבא, ומ"מ בדרך רחוקה הוא, שאין יכול ליכנס בשעת שחיטה, דהיינו כל שש שעות עד שקיעת החמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:5:1.english: [They] slaughtered [it] and sprinkled [its blood] on his behalf - And in the evening he will arrive, and nevertheless he is [considered to be] on a distant journey, since he cannot enter [Jerusalem] at the time of slaughter, which is all six hours [from midday] until sunset.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:5:2.english: [His offering] was accepted - and [he is] exempt from the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:5:3.hebrew: כטמא - ולא עשה כלום, וזקוק לשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:5:3.english: Like one who is ritually impure - And he has accomplished nothing, and he is obligated [to observe] the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:7:1.hebrew: מדקתני ולא עשה מכלל דאי בעי מצי עביד - ואטמא ליכא לאוקמא, ועל כרחיך אדרך רחוקה קא מהדר:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:7:1.english: From the fact that it teaches, "and did not observe," [it follows] by inference that had he wished, he could have observed [it] - And it cannot be established regarding one who was ritually impure, so perforce it refers back to [one on] a distant journey.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:8:1.hebrew: וליטעמיך, סיפא גבי שגג ונאנס, דתנא תו זימנא אחריתי "ולא עשה", אהי מוקמת לה? הלא שגג ולא ידע שהיום פסח, הרי שגג ונאנס, ומאי "אי בעי" איכא למימר הכא? אלא מאי אית לך למימר בלא עשה דסיפא? מזיד קתני בהדייהו, ועלה קאי "ולא עשה", דאי בעי הוה עביד:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:8:1.english: And according to your reasoning, the latter clause [of the Mishnah] regarding one who acted unwittingly or was prevented [by circumstances beyond his control], where it teaches yet another time "and he did not observe [it]" — to which [case] do you apply it? Did he not act unwittingly and not know that today is Pesach? Behold, he acted unwittingly or was prevented, so what [inference of] "if he wished" can be said here? Rather, what must you say regarding "and he did not observe [it]" in the latter clause? It teaches [the case of] one who acted intentionally together with them, and it is to that [case] that "and he did not observe [it]" refers, for had he wished, he would have observed [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:8:2.hebrew: ה"נ - גבי לא עשה דרישא, אונן קתני בהדייהו, ועלה קאי "ולא עשה", דאי בעי עביד, כדאמרי' בפ' האשה (דף צא.): האונן והמפקח הגל כו' שוחטין עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 92b:8:2.english: Here too - Regarding "and he did not observe" in the first clause [of the Mishnah], [it] teaches [the case of] an acute mourner together with them, and "and he did not observe" refers to that [case], for if he wished he could have observed [it], as we say in the chapter HaIsha (91a): For an acute mourner and one who clears away a heap [of rubble], etc., we slaughter [the Paschal offering] on their behalf.

Rashi on Pesachim 92b:9:1.english: [The Mishnah] is also precise - That it teaches [about] an intentional [transgressor] and an acute mourner in it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:1:1.hebrew: בודקין לעושי פסח - וא"ת: דמשמע הכא דווקא לעושי פסח התירו ע"י בדיקה, משום דלא העמידו דבריהם במקום כרת, ובפ' בכל מערבין (עירובין ד' כו:) תנן: "מערבין לכהן בבית הפרס", ומפרש בגמרא: משום דמצי אזיל כדרב יהודה! ואומר ר"י: דהאי דקאמר הכא "במקום כרת" דוקא, היינו משום דאיכא נמי כרת בעשיית פסח בטומא', והיינו דקאמר בסוף חגיגה (דף כה:): "לעושי פסח לא העמידו דבריהם במקום כרת, לאוכלי תרומה העמידו דבריהם במקום מיתה". פירוש: לענין פסח טיהרוהו, אע"ג דאיכא כרת באכילתו בטומאה; לענין תרומה העמידו דבריהם ולא טיהרוהו, אע"ג דליכא אלא מיתה לאוכלה בטומאה; אבל בטומאת כהן, דליכא אלא לאו, שרי ליכנס בבית הפרס לצורך עירוב. ויש דבר, כגון ללמוד תורה ולישא אשה, דשרי אפי' בלא נפוח, כדאמרי' במי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מז.) ובע"א (דף יג.), משום דעדיפי משאר מצות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:1:1.english: "We examine for those offering the Paschal lamb" - And if you ask: Here it implies that specifically for those offering the Paschal lamb did [the Sages] permit [entering a beit haperas] by means of examination, because they did not uphold their [rabbinic] words in the face of karet; yet in the chapter Bekhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 26b) we learned [in the Mishnah]: "One may place an eruv for a Kohen in a beit haperas," and the Gemara explains: because he can go in accordance with [the ruling of] Rav Yehudah [by blowing on the ground before each step]! And R. Yitzchak says: That which it says here "in the face of karet" specifically is because there is also karet for offering the Paschal lamb in impurity, and this is what it says at the end of Chagigah (25b): "For those offering the Paschal lamb they did not uphold their words in the face of karet; for those eating terumah they upheld their words in the face of death [at the hands of Heaven]." Explanation: Regarding the Paschal lamb they declared him pure [via examination], even though there is karet for eating it in impurity; regarding terumah they upheld their words and did not declare him pure, even though there is only death [at the hands of Heaven] for eating it in impurity; however, regarding the impurity of a Kohen, where there is only a negative commandment, it is permitted [for him] to enter a beit haperas [by blowing] for the purpose of an eruv. And there is a matter — such as to study Torah or to marry a wife — where it is permitted even without blowing, as we say in [the chapter] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (Eruvin 47a) and in Avodah Zarah (13a), because they are superior to other mitzvot.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:2:1.hebrew: מאי בודקין - קשה לר"ת: מאי קבעי? הלא הבדיקה מפורשת בסוף אהלות באותה משנה עצמה, דקתני: "ומודים ב"ש וב"ה שבודקין לעושי פסח, ואין בודקין לאוכלי תרומ'; ולנזיר — ב"ש אומרים בודקין, וב"ה אומרים אין בודקין. כיצד הוא עושה? מביא את העפר שהוא יכול להסיטו, ונותן לתוך כברה שנקביה דקים כו'". ואומר ר"י, דבדיקה דמתני' — בשכבר עבר, ורב יהודה ורב חייא באין לפרש שיוכל לבא ולעבור; וה"ק: מאי בודקין אם רצה לעבור: [עי' תוספות בכורות כט. ד"ה היכי אזיל כו', וע"ע תוס כתובות כח: ד"ה מנפח]:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:2:1.english: What is [meant by] "we examine" - Rabbeinu Tam finds [this] difficult: What is [the Gemara] asking? Is the examination not explicitly stated at the end of Ohalot, in that very Mishnah itself, where it teaches: "And Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree that one may examine [a beit haperas] for those offering the Paschal lamb, and one may not examine for those eating terumah; and for a nazirite — Beit Shammai say one may examine, and Beit Hillel say one may not examine. How does he do it? He brings the earth that he is able to move, and puts [it] into a sieve whose holes are fine, etc."? And Ri says that the examination of the Mishnah [applies] where he has already passed through [it], whereas Rav Yehuda and Rav Chiya come to explain [how one examines] so that he may come and pass through [it]; and this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "How do we examine" if one wishes to pass through [it]: [See Tosafot on Bekhorot 29a, s.v. Heikhi azil, etc., and see further Tosafot on Ketubot 28b, s.v. Menapei'ach]:

Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:4:1.hebrew: מי שהיה טמא. אלו פטורין מהכרת - נראה לר"י דמתני' קסבר: שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ, והשתא איירי מתניתין בטמא מת בששי, דלא חזי לאכילה לאורתא; דאי קסבר אין שוחטין, אם כן טמא דמתני' — אף בטמא שרץ, או דטמא מת בשביעי שלו, א"כ אמאי פטור מהכרת כיון דיכול לטבול? דהתניא בפ' אלו דברים (לעיל פסחים דף סט:): "יכול לא יהא ענוש כרת אלא טהור ושלא היה בדרך רחוקה; ערל וטמא שרץ ושאר טמאים מנין? ת"ל: 'והאיש'", ומשמע דליכא מאן דפליג עלה, מדפריך מינה לרבא דקאמר דר"א פוטר מכרת. וא"ת: תיקשי מתני' לרב, דאמר לעיל (פסחים דף צ:): אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ? וי"ל: דכמה תנאי אשכחן דסברי כרב דאין שוחטין; והא דפריך ליה לעיל ממתניתין דזב שראה שתי ראיות, היינו משום דרב עלה קאי ומוקי לה בשטבל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:4:1.english: One who was [ritually] impure. These are exempt from karet - It appears to Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that our Mishnah holds [that] we slaughter [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkle [its blood] on behalf of one who is impure from a creeping animal [sheretz], and accordingly our Mishnah is dealing with one who is impure from a corpse on the sixth [day], who is not fit to eat [the offering] in the evening. For if it holds [that] we do not slaughter [and sprinkle for him], if so, "impure" in our Mishnah [would apply] even to one impure from a creeping animal, or to one impure from a corpse on his seventh [day]; if so, why is he exempt from karet, since he can immerse [and become pure by evening]? For it was taught in a baraita in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Devarim (above, Pesachim 69b): "One might [think] that only one who was pure and not on a distant journey is punishable by karet; [as for] an uncircumcised person, one impure from a creeping animal, and other impure people, from where [do we know they are liable]? The verse states: 'But the man [veha'ish].'" And it is implied that there is no one who disagrees with this [baraita], from the fact that [the Gemara] objects from it to Rava, who said that Rabbi Eliezer exempts [them] from karet. And if you ask: Let our Mishnah pose a difficulty to Rav, who said above (Pesachim 90b) that we do not slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of one who is impure from a creeping animal? One can answer: We find several Tanna'im who hold like Rav that we do not slaughter [and sprinkle for him]; and that which [the Gemara] objected to him above from the Mishnah of "a zav who saw two sightings" — that is because Rav was standing on [that Mishnah] and establishes it as referring to where he had [already] immersed.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:5:1.hebrew: ורב נחמן אמר הורצה - רב נחמן מצי סבר כרב יהודה, דאמר לקמן: דרך רחוקה — כל שאין יכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה, ואפ"ה הורצה; דנהי דאינו יכול בהילוך בינוני, כיון דיכול לבא בסוסים ובפרדים, בר אכילה הוא, ולא דמי לחולה וערל וטמא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:5:1.english: And Rav Nachman said: [His offering] was accepted - Rav Nachman can hold like Rav Yehuda, who says later [on]: "A distant journey" [means] any [distance from which] one cannot enter [Jerusalem] by the time of eating [the Paschal offering], and even so [his offering] was accepted; for although he cannot [arrive] at an average walking pace, since he can come on horses and on mules, he is fit for eating [it], and he is not comparable to a sick person, an uncircumcised person, or a ritually impure person.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:8:1.hebrew: הכא נמי אונן קתני בהדייהו - וא"ת: מה בין אונן למזיד (ושוגג), דאם הוא מזיד — היינו מזיד, (ואם הוא שוגג) — היינו שוגג? וי"ל: דתנא תרי גווני מזיד; חד שהניח בחנם, ואונן שנתעצל אגב מרריה. ומיירי במת לו מת אחר חצות, אבל קודם חצות אינו בהכרת, כדמוכח בסוף פירקין, וכן איתא בהדיא בפ' טבול יום (זבחים דף ק.). ולעיל הוי מצי למיחשב נמי אונן בהדי הנהו דהעמידו דבריהם, במת קודם חצות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92b:8:1.english: Here, too, [the Mishnah] teaches [the case of] an acute mourner (onen) together with them - And if you ask: What is the difference between an acute mourner and one who acted intentionally (and one who acted unwittingly)? For if he acted intentionally, that is [the case of] "intentional" (and if he acted unwittingly, that is [the case of] "unwitting")! And one can answer: [The Tanna] taught two types of intentional [abstention]: one who neglected [it] without cause, and an acute mourner who was negligent due to his bitterness [of grief]. And [this] refers to where his relative died after midday; however, [if he died] before midday, he is not subject to karet, as is proven at the end of our chapter, and so it is stated explicitly in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (Zevachim 100a). And earlier [in the sugya], [the Gemara] could also have counted an acute mourner among those [cases where the Sages] upheld their words, in a case where [the relative] died before midday:
